title: The Global Screening Array

blocks.what_we_do: Recognise what an array includes and what it leaves unmeasured.
blocks.why: The Illumina Global Screening Array (GSA) targets a selected set of sites. It is not whole-genome sequencing: an unmeasured site cannot be called absent. The simulated course subset uses GSA-style Illumina names and real GRCh38 positions. The local manufacturer manifest is not redistributed. The student annotation supplies only the fields needed for this course; it does not reproduce the full proprietary design.
blocks.command:
```{r s1-3}
table(ann$Chr)
stopifnot(nrow(ann) == 299523L, !anyDuplicated(ann$Name))
```

blocks.expected_result:
Autosomes 1 to 22 plus X, Y and MT. There are 299,523 initial array entries; duplicated genomic sites can have distinct names and will be reviewed at 4.5.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with the supplied simulated dataset.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
If a site is absent from the array, can you conclude that every participant has the reference allele there?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Absence from the array means the site was not directly measured.

</details>
